title: A multi-word = query in quick search is a substring compare, so a longer title matches what the manual calls an exact match
statement: Quick search's leading = is documented as an exact match on the title or content. For a single word it behaves that way, but when the compared value contains a space the comparator falls into a branch that returns normalizedVal.includes(normalizedCompared), a substring test. A note titled "Tchello17 world extra" therefore matches the query =Tchello17 world. Adding a space silently changes the semantics from equals to contains.

handVerified.note: Report section 4. Control (a) is the discriminator: with notes 'Tcsolo17' and 'Tcsolo17extra' both present, =Tcsolo17 returns only the exact one, so the operator, the route and the titles are all fine for a single word. The comparator source was confirmed verbatim including the comment stating the intent.

source.howDecided: No commit touches build_comparator.ts between the tested commit and head; the blob is identical at tested, head and v0.105.0. Re-read at head: the '=' comparator at :15-32 still contains `if (normalizedCompared.includes(" ")) return normalizedVal.includes(normalizedCompared);` at :26-28. Open PR #10633 rewrites this operator to strict normalised full-value equality (`"=": (comparedValue) => (val) => normalizeSearchText(val) === normalizeSearchText(comparedValue)`) and moves the old word/phrase behaviour to an internal, non-user-typable "word=" operator that parse.ts uses only for the leading-'=' fulltext title path, so that PR does fix this finding.

citedItems.note: Read in full this pass: labels Type: Documentation and search, filed against 0.102.2, last updated 2026-05-02. It quotes the same manual lines the report quotes and states the behaviour accurately in the reporter's own words ('=A B match either exact A or exact B, again as part of the target text'), so it genuinely covers this finding rather than a sliver of it. It frames the question as docs-versus-implementation and does not name build_comparator.ts, which is the only thing the report adds.
Confirmed at the file level to change '=' to strict full-value equality; it also updates both Quick search.md and Search.md, which is the documentation half of #9422.

queries: gh search issues --repo TriliumNext/Trilium 'exact match operator title equals'

reevaluation: The finding still reproduces on main and in v0.105.0, but it is both accurately reported (#9422, open) and fixed in a clean, actively updated open PR (#10633, which also rewrites the two doc pages). Nothing moved since the report and nothing new was filed. The report's only increment over #9422 is naming the line, and #10633 already changed that line, so a new issue or a comment would add close to nothing and would spend account credit that FILING-GUIDE says is finite. If #10633 stalls, the correct follow-up is a comment on #9422 pointing at build_comparator.ts:26-28, not a new issue.
